No woman should ever face charges for her pregnancy outcome, and no doctor should be criminalized for providing proper care.

@DemWomenCaucus and I sent a letter to @POTUS urging him to protect patients & doctors from Republicans' attempts to criminalize women's pregnancies. https://t.co/Nmg2ezNWHR

Republicans aren’t happy enough with subjecting women to arduous journeys to access reproductive health care or criminalizing doctors for providing care to their patients.

Now, they are expanding their plan to strip away the most personal decisions a family can make. (1/2)

Today marks two years since Russia's brutal, unprovoked, and full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

This week marks the 14th anniversary of the #AffordableCareAct!

From lowering costs, to expanding coverage, and improving maternal health, the #ACA has made health care more affordable for millions of Americans.

For decades, federal law has ensured hospitals provide the necessary emergency care—including abortion care—that patients need.

Now, with this protection under full attack, I joined my colleagues in urging the Supreme Court to protect life-saving care.
https://t.co/EEBIMSzFtd

For decades, federal law has required hospitals to provide the necessary emergency care—including abortion—that patients need. Yet today, the Supreme Court is hearing Idaho's case threatening those rights.
 
I'm calling on the Court to protect the life-saving care our women need.

The Global Gag Rule is a cruel attack on women’s health; it blocks U.S. global health funding to international organizations that use their own money to provide abortion services or even simply share reproductive health care information with their patients.

I introduced the Global HER Act with 100+ colleagues to permanently repeal this harmful policy and promote healthier, more prosperous communities worldwide.

For 15 years, the Affordable Care Act has lowered costs, expanded coverage, and protected millions with preexisting conditions. Thanks to the ACA, 4 out of 5 Americans can get a health plan for $10 or less.

@HouseDemocrats won’t let Republicans gut this progress.

Firing thousands of career public servants—not political appointees—who track infectious diseases, inspect food and hospitals, and oversee health insurance programs for half the country isn’t just reckless.

It’s dangerous. And it won’t lower our costs.
